primitives.name: Hierarchical Bayesian Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: RESEARCH A Hierarchical Bayesian Model for Cyber-Human Assessment of Rehabilitation Movement Tamim Ahmed1*†, Thanassis Rikakis2, Setor Zilevu3, Aisling Kelliher3, Kowshik Thopalli4, Pavan Turaga4 and Steven L.
primitives.assumptions: Bayes' theorem, conditional independence, conjugate priors, Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-convergence due to insufficient data or poor prior specification.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Probabilistic fusion of clinician and automated assessments. GSE: State-transition modeling of recovery trajectories.
layer2.telemetry: Posterior predictive checks, cross-validation error, Kullback-Leibler divergence.

primitives.name: Automated Assessment Ensemble
primitives.verbatim_quote: The automated assessment ensemble integrates expert knowledge constraints into data driven training though a combination of HMM, transformer, MSTCN++, and decision tree computational modules.
primitives.assumptions: Data stationarity, module calibration, decision threshold optimality.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overfitting due to high-dimensional kinematic data or class imbalance.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Multi-model fusion for robust kinematic analysis. GSE: Ensemble prediction for recovery trajectory forecasting.
layer2.telemetry: F1-score, precision-recall curve, confusion matrix metrics.

primitives.name: K-Means Clustering
primitives.verbatim_quote: Finally, we used k-means clustering on the ∆HBM to identify three clusters of features among the 16 movement composite and 20 kinematic features and used the centroid of these clusters as the weights of the input data to our computational assessment ensemble.
primitives.assumptions: Spherical cluster shapes, equal variance, Euclidean distance metric.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Suboptimal centroid initialization leading to local minima.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Feature weighting and dimensionality reduction for predictive modeling. GSE: State partitioning for policy optimization.
layer2.telemetry: Silhouette score, elbow method gap statistics, within-cluster sum of squares.

primitives.name: Correlation Graph
primitives.verbatim_quote: We increased the granularity of observation of the HBM by formulating ∆HBM, a correlation graph between kinematics and movement composite features.
primitives.assumptions: Linear relationships, multivariate normal distribution, no multicollinearity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Spurious correlations from confounding variables or small sample sizes.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Network analysis of biomechanical interactions. GSE: Causal graph representation for intervention planning.
layer2.telemetry: Pearson/Spearman correlation coefficients, partial correlation matrices, network centrality measures.

reasoning_traces.think:
The hierarchical Bayesian model (HBM) provides a rigorous probabilistic framework to quantify the uncertainty inherent in both clinician ratings and automated kinematic analysis. By incorporating expert knowledge as prior distributions, the model ensures interpretability while leveraging large-scale data for posterior inference. The automated assessment ensemble acts as a derived kernel within the HBM, translating raw sensor data into clinically relevant scores. K-means clustering serves as a veto mechanism, preventing overfitting by reducing the dimensionality of the feature space and enforcing orthogonality among input variables. The correlation graph visualizes the resulting posterior dependencies, enabling clinicians to understand how specific kinematic features map onto functional outcomes. Together, these primitives form a closed-loop system where each component validates and constrains the others, ensuring robustness against noise and variability.
